concepts.title: Rise of Chhatrapati Shivaji
concepts.definition: Chhatrapati Shivaji carved an independent Maratha kingdom out of the Deccan in the seventeenth century by seizing hill forts, building a disciplined army and navy, and crowning himself sovereign king in 1674, challenging the might of the Adil Shahi sultans and the Mughals.
concepts.key_idea: Hill forts, swift cavalry and clever diplomacy built a Maratha state under Shivaji.

solution_steps.explain: Shivaji began with small bands and the hill forts of western Maharashtra.
A loyal army, navy, fort network and tax system gave the kingdom its frame.
The 1674 coronation declared an independent sovereign Maratha state.

concepts.title: Shivaji's Administration and the Sovereign King
concepts.definition: Shivaji ran his kingdom through an organised council of eight ministers, collected fair taxes, kept his forces disciplined even inside enemy territory, and styled himself a sovereign king serving his people - the famous royal ideal recorded in his counsel to his son.
concepts.key_idea: A council of ministers, fair revenue and people-first rule made the Maratha state durable.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees103.txt lines 552-806 (the sovereign king, counsel and administration)

solution_steps.explain: Eight ministers headed departments from finance to foreign affairs.
Assessment of land and fair collection funded the state without crushing peasants.
The king's letters counselled protecting subjects, especially farmers and women.

concepts.title: The Marathas after Shivaji
concepts.definition: After Shivaji's death his son Sambhaji and successors carried the struggle against Mughal expansion; under the Peshwas in the eighteenth century the Maratha confederacy of houses like Scindia, Holkar, Gaekwad and Bhonsle spread Maratha influence across most of India.
concepts.key_idea: From a Deccan kingdom to an all-India confederacy - Maratha power kept growing after 1680.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees103.txt lines 423-550 (the Marathas after Chhatrapati Shivaji)

solution_steps.explain: Sambhaji and Rajaram kept the anti-Mughal resistance alive.
Peshwa leadership from Pune guided expansion northwards.
Scindia, Holkar, Gaekwad and Bhonsle families held regions under a shared banner.

concepts.title: Maratha Legacy and centres like Thanjavur
concepts.definition: The Marathas left a lasting legacy in administration, military organisation and culture - patronising temples and learning, and ruling centres such as Thanjavur, where Maratha kings supported art, music and scholarship well into the colonial era.
concepts.key_idea: Maratha rule shaped polity and culture alike, from hill forts to Thanjavur's courts.

The southern court of Thanjavur kept Maratha culture alive far from the Deccan.
